leading_positions.synthesis: All eight round-1 files name B009 as the preferred single-part configuration, credited to Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye. Shared: Katori's magic-wavelength lattice is a separable, original invention; Ye's group carried it to roughly 1e-18 uncertainty and many-body-aware operation; the result has been reproduced independently in Sr and Yb laboratories and underpins tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and the discussion of a redefinition of the second. Not shared: the weight each member gives to the category question (discovery versus metrology instrument), to the 2005 and 2012 precedents, and to the credit owed to other groups; and the citation wording, which varies (magic-wavelength trapping appears in the Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson citations, the 1e-18 level in the Eriksson, Johansson, Lindroth, Mehlig and Pearce citations, a 'new regime' of precision in the Danielsson and Kroll citations, and the Olsson citation names neither precision nor 1e-18). Several members moved to this position from lower opening ranks (Danielsson 5th, Eriksson 5th), and Eriksson and Danielsson say they moved because of colleagues' attribution and maturity arguments, so the unanimity partly reflects movement after the opening ballots; Olsson and Pearce each name a different first-ranked opening candidate (B017 and B052) as an alternative rather than as their preferred configuration.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members prefer B009 with exactly the two names Katori and Ye; no member proposes a different or larger set of laureates for this configuration, and no member proposes a second prize part.
All eight describe Katori's magic-wavelength trapping as the distinct conceptual step, and Ye's group as the route to the roughly 1e-18 frontier and many-body clock physics.

All eight cite independent reproduction in several laboratories and species, and concrete uses (fundamental-constant tests, relativistic geodesy, dark-matter and new-physics searches, the possible redefinition of the second).

Every member lists the same reservations, in some form: category (metrology versus discovery), overlap with the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and credit to groups outside the two names.

Seven members list B018 (topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect) among their stated alternatives (Danielsson, Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce); this is a listed alternative and not a stated preference for B018 over B009.
scientific_disputes: Whether an optical lattice clock is a discovery-class advance or precision instrumentation. Danielsson and Eriksson say they were or remain lukewarm on this point and note that B018, B010 or B052 open new questions rather than sharpen a measurement; Johansson, Lindroth and Olsson treat the magic-wavelength idea as a distinct conceptual step; Eriksson says B009 would drop if the committee prefers a change in what physicists can think about over what they can measure.

How much of the scientific payoff is delivered and how much is prospective. Danielsson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Pearce note that dark-matter searches, geodesy or the redefinition of the second are projected; Eriksson and Lindroth emphasise concrete delivered consequences. Danielsson states that the clocks have not yet produced a fundamental-physics result of their own.

Alternatives differ in kind: B018 (seven members list it), B014 (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth), B052 (Danielsson, Pearce), and single mentions of B008 (Johansson), B010 (Mehlig), B017 (Olsson) and B041 (Eriksson). Eriksson states that no one but he ranked B041 highly, and Danielsson notes that B052 was ranked by only three members with Olsson placing it seventh because the origin of most of the neutrino flux is unresolved.
attribution_disputes: Whether two names fairly represent lattice-clock history. Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson name Lemonde, Ludlow, Hinkley, Lisdat or the PTB, NIST, Yb and Hg groups as contributors who would be excluded by a Katori-Ye citation; Danielsson, Johansson and Kroll also point to Gill and the ion-clock and frequency-comb lineage. No member proposes adding names; the question is whether the citation wording can carry the narrower claim.

For B018, Danielsson, Johansson and Lindroth note that the Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposal and the three-dimensional topological-insulator work fall outside the three supplied names Kane, Mele and Molenkamp.

For B052, Danielsson, Olsson and Pearce say credit among Halzen, Karle and Spiering, and relative to the AMANDA, Baikal and DUMAND precursors and the large collaboration, is unsettled; Pearce regards his own three-name proposal as the weaker part of his opening case.
For B014 and B010, Lindroth asks how Zoller would be treated if both remained in contention.
maturity_disputes: Whether to wait for the redefinition of the second, which has not been decided. Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce raise it explicitly as a timing question; Johansson, Eriksson and Mehlig cite the redefinition discussion as evidence that clocks are already measurement infrastructure.

For B052, Pearce says source identification is still at moderate significance and he does not insist on IceCube this year; Danielsson says the diffuse flux is established and should not be held hostage to source associations, though he now wants more discussion of credit.
Danielsson cautions that broad opening support for B009 (all eight ranked it, six in the top three) should not be mistaken for depth of scientific weight.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Kroll (disclosed): a research period during doctoral studies in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, where Jun Ye also trained, and work in atomic physics and laser spectroscopy at Lund; he describes this as a professional connection, not a stake, and says the committee may wish to consider it. Danielsson also asks that it be noted when B009 is discussed. Kroll also notes that B014 (Cirac-Zoller) is adjacent to his work on quantum memories.

Johansson (disclosed): directs WACQT at Chalmers and works on superconducting circuits, so B008 is in his own field and he would recuse on any decision turning on B008; no connection to Katori, Ye or other candidates is apparent.

Olsson (disclosed): first-ranked B017 in the opening, works in transmission electron microscopy and is reported as IFSM president in 2024; she lists B017 only as a secondary alternative and would accept recusal from any B017 decision. Johansson is noted as a Chalmers colleague.
Lindroth (disclosed): atomic theorist, so B009, B014 and B010 lie in her broad field; she flags a disciplinary bias and notes her documented collaborators are not credited names.
Eriksson (disclosed): adjacent electronic-structure work near B041 and B018, a reason he treats his own earlier B041 ranking with caution.

Pearce (chair, disclosed): astroparticle experimentalist at KTH whose profile records no IceCube membership or tie to the credited names; the field proximity to B052 is noted, no recusal is recommended, and no connection to B009 is recorded.
Danielsson and Mehlig report no specific conflict.
questions_for_round2: Should the committee treat the optical lattice clock as a discovery-class advance or as precision instrumentation, and what in the 2005 and 2012 citations distinguishes the proposed award from them?

Can a citation be worded so it credits Katori for the magic-wavelength lattice and Ye for the accuracy and many-body frontier, and states explicitly what it does not credit (other Sr, Yb and Hg groups, ion clocks, combs)?
Should the 1e-18 accuracy level, magic-wavelength trapping, or both appear in the citation, given that the five round-1 wordings differ on this?
Does the redefinition of the second, not yet decided, bear on timing, and would any member change position if it were or were not completed?
Does Kroll's disclosed Boulder connection to the Hall laboratory require recusal, abstention or only recording, and do other members consider it material?
What delivered fundamental-physics result, as distinct from prospective use, can each supporter cite for lattice clocks?
For members listing B018 as an alternative, would they prefer it over B009 if the Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and 3D omissions were resolved, and on what scientific basis?
For B052, what would settle credit among Halzen, Karle and Spiering relative to AMANDA, Baikal and DUMAND, and is the diffuse-flux discovery alone, without source identification, sufficient?
summary.chair_observation: All eight round-1 files prefer the same single-part B009 configuration with the same two names, which leaves round 2 with a narrow agenda: the discovery-versus-metrology question, the citation wording and its limits on credit, the timing relative to the redefinition of the second, and the handling of Kroll's disclosed connection. Seven of the eight alternatives lists include B018. Alternatives are listed explicitly but only as secondary choices, so the files do not show a rival configuration, and the unanimity is partly the product of movement after the opening ballots that members themselves describe, which round 2 should test rather than assume.
